question: Does ordinary admission cap2, with all requests actually arriving and completing, remove the group/phase-transition cost more effectively than immediate admission?
hypothesis: Delaying never-started work may preserve the incumbent working set and move prefill until slots release. Incoming queueing is fully charged; finishing-old release of prefill to native budget64 is a separate simple baseline.

runtime.chunk: 32; release arm threshold0 after old completion, effective64

event: Same two-old-token prefix and event after four outputs each. All three arms really submit the third request with the same event arrival rule; its waiting time is included in TTFT.
costs: Same observation wrapper and five common warmup variants plus drained warmup; actual allocations/peaks and all request time retained. Map validation after capture; all reset/flush/IO/shutdown recorded in engine/parent cycle.
prestate: Source-ID normalized logical metadata including output tokens, positions, KV counts and pager slots/LRU. Physical KV IDs retained separately; no KV tensor equality claim.
scope: Already observed triplet, six same-engine cells. The two incumbents have equal fixed output length and advance synchronously, so both finish on the same step in these admission baselines. This is a bounded causal/strong-baseline probe, not evidence across heterogeneous lengths or continuous arrivals.
stops: Foreign GPU or query failure, source mismatch, missing/dropped requests, old decode fails to advance, unexpected KV/preemption/waiting state, incorrect release/budget/restoration or accounting aborts and retains the attempt.
comparison: D minus I, R minus I, R minus D within each block; all metrics and same-arm repeated drift. No prior-campaign absolute timing comparison, no empirically observed maximum used as noise bound.
continuation: If a simple admission baseline resolves this case, retain it as the strong baseline and test fresh heterogeneous requests/clock arrivals. If waiting offsets saving, model the actual queue/phase transition without rescuing RR by threshold tuning. No arbitrary gain threshold or problem-family kill.
ordering: Declared immediate32,admit2_32,admit2_release64 then reverse; not independent randomized blocks.
action: After common prestate snapshot, I keeps max_num_running_reqs3; D/R set it2. Native scheduler alone assigns KV and advances all admitted decode requests. R after both old requests complete sets long_prefill_token_threshold0, still bounded by actual native token budget64. On exit restore cap3/threshold32/token execution.
required_costs: new actual queue waiting and first scheduled time
